doc.title: Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Oneonta, New York, December 28, 2005

title: Remaking Czardas and Hora Staccato; Brahms quintet
summary: Rerecording faster seven years later, plus the live 1964 Brahms quintet.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: I have to tell you this story. JoAnn, you know it. “Saxophone Contrasts” I recorded Czardas Monti and Hora Staccato. Both excellent. Even I like it. Now I want you to understand what that means, even I like it. That is not egotism, that’s perfectionism. When I say even I like it, I’m very particular with myself. Okay. Now seven years later they wanted me to do another album. And they wanted me to do the Hora Staccato and the Czardas again. I said man I did a beautiful job on the Columbia. I’ve got to do it both as well and faster. So nobody, none of the musicians can say, “Well Gallodoro sort of slowed up a little.” No. You listen to both. They’re going to be both on there. They are both a little faster and a little better. But I was in my prime.
As that guy on the CD said from that radio broadcast, he said, “That was some mighty fine tootin.’”
I’m so thrilled to have this opportunity. I look forward to hearing about all your future appearances and so forth.

Just let me say that all of the CDs there, you don’t hear all of my playing. Because with the group that I had when I first met you at the Alley, I was playing different you know. But all-in-all, you can hear from jazz to classical. The Brahms “Clarinet Quintet” that was done live back in 1964. Live at ABC. It’s just perfect as I could have gotten it even if I had gone into a studio. Oh yes. And the one I did in Florida with the 16-year-old boy.
